text: Gold slipped about 0.7% to near $3,856 after touching about $3,830, its lowest since October 2025, as a firm dollar and Fed hike bets weighed; Fed Chair Warsh's speech gave no clear hint on December.
Silver fell about 3.6% to a 52-week low near $46.90, lifting the gold/silver ratio to about 82; SLV closed down 3.9% at $42.39 and AGQ down 7.9% at $39.10.
Gold miners fell much more than gold: GDX lost 3.3% to $78.95 and GDXJ 3.7% to $95.35.

The Nasdaq fell 2.5% and the S&P 500 1.9%, a third straight drop, as Nvidia hit its lowest close since July 2025 and new US rules limited remote access to advanced chips; QQQ fell 2.7%, TQQQ 8.1%, and SQQQ rose 8.1%.
The VIX jumped about 19% to 22.9, its biggest one-day rise since Nov 5.
Brent crude fell about 3.5% to $92.44 as the IEA's surplus outlook outweighed reports of tanker fires in the Strait of Hormuz.
Treasury yields eased (10-year near 5.12%, 2-year near 4.82%), while the dollar index rose to 103.58, its highest close since April 2025; USD/JPY edged down to about 159.4.
